_description: Performance baseline for issue #391 PERFORMANCE slice (4 boxes: cascade BFS / HybridRetriever / BM25 rebuild / Postgres slow log). All six baselines are CI-blessed from workflow_dispatch runs (see per-box _blessed_from_ci_runs): cascade_5hop_bfs + bm25_build_1k/5k/10k on the feat/403-perf-baseline-rebless branch (#403), and the two HybridRetriever baselines (p50/p95) against a local pgvector substrate (#414; deterministic embedder + the real hybrid_*_search SQL functions, no Supabase/OpenAI secrets). The harness compares current p50/p95 wall-clock against these baselines and fails on regression beyond the documented tolerance band. Real production targets are listed in _target_* fields for reference; baseline mean_ms values reflect the CI runner shape, not the absolute targets. When re-blessing a baseline, replicate the 3-run methodology (workflow_dispatch on the rebless branch) and update _blessed_from_ci_runs to match.
_methodology: Each of the 3 CI workflow_dispatch runs above ran scripts/run_benchmarks.sh against the in-memory _FakeSupabaseGraph (cascade) + reference BM25 builder (bm25). Per-run median_ms is captured in test-results/measurements-*.json artifacts on each run; the baseline mean_ms below is the median-of-medians across the 3 runs (median across runs = primary statistic; stdev across runs reported in _observed_variance_pct). Tolerance band derivation (codex iter-2 closure of M1): relative band = 10% safety floor (~5-7x observed stdev), absolute band = ~2x observed full-timing range rounded up to nearest 5ms (min 5ms floor); the comparison helper uses max(rel_band, abs_band) so each box's effective band is also tracked explicitly in _effective_band_pct for review-time honesty. 2026-08-06 amendment (issue #1502): the bm25 absolute bands were re-derived from a fleet-aware 9-run sample (see _bm25_band_recalibration) because the original 3 blessing runs landed on similar hardware and under-sampled GitHub-hosted-runner fleet variance; mean_ms values were NOT re-blessed (the fleet sample's med-of-meds sat within 1.1% of every blessed center).

_bm25_band_recalibration._method: 9 CI runs on identical code/corpus/baseline (3 organic runs from the 2026-08-06 incident window + 6 workflow_dispatch runs on main in 3 waves of 2 over ~30min) sampled distinct runner hardware: one uniformly ~9% slower machine (31059008024), one with a size-dependent +12.8% elevation at 10k only (31063489593, the spurious-REGRESSION run), and one uniformly ~20-23% FASTER machine (31065595212). Because the comparison gate is one-sided (observed <= baseline auto-passes as improvement), the fast-machine outlier widens the raw min-max range in a direction that can never fail the gate; the band is therefore derived from the failure-relevant spread instead: abs band = 2x the max observed run-median elevation above the blessed center, rounded up to nearest 5ms, min 5ms floor (same 2x multiplier + rounding as #403, applied to the slow side the gate actually judges). Per-slice: 1k max elevation +1.59ms -> 2x=3.2 -> 5ms floor (unchanged); 5k +9.78ms -> 2x=19.6 -> 20ms; 10k +28.45ms -> 2x=56.9 -> 60ms. Cross-run stdev of run medians was 8.3-9.1% on all three slices (vs 1.4-1.9% in the 3-run blessing) — fleet variance, not code, dominates. Re-bless/re-derive procedure: >=6 workflow_dispatch runs dispatched in waves spread over hours (ideally days) so distinct runner hardware classes are sampled; 3 back-to-back runs are NOT a sufficient sample.

cascade_5hop_bfs._target_rationale: Issue #391 PERFORMANCE box 1: '< 500ms for 5-hop BFS'. Synthetic graph shape may not match production graph; tolerance band is relative to blessed baseline, not the absolute target.
cascade_5hop_bfs._ci_observation: 3 CI runs (workflow_dispatch on feat/403-perf-baseline-rebless) produced per-run median_ms [352.54, 357.23, 363.27]; med-of-meds=357.23ms, stdev across runs=5.38ms (1.51%), range across 15 individual timings=20.09ms (345.95–366.04). p95 across runs was tight (med-of-p95s=365.41ms). The synthetic in-memory _FakeSupabaseGraph traverses ~1000 reachable nodes per cascade so absolute numbers reflect Python-side BFS overhead on the ubuntu-latest CI runner, NOT real Supabase round-trips. The 500ms absolute target remains the documentation anchor for an eventual real-Postgres measurement.
cascade_5hop_bfs._tolerance_rationale: 10% relative OR 45ms absolute (whichever wider). Comparison helper takes max(rel, abs) so effective band is 45ms = 12.6% of baseline (rel band 35.72ms is dominated by abs floor; 8.3x observed stdev/med = 1.51%). Absolute band 45ms = ~2x observed full-timing range (20.09ms across 15 samples in 3 runs), rounded up to nearest 5ms. Narrowed from the pre-#403 100ms placeholder (28% effective) per codex iter-2 M1 (honest derivation: abs floor should be close to observed range, not 5x it).

hybrid_retriever_search_p50._target_rationale: Issue #391 PERFORMANCE box 2: '< 200ms for fused search'. Live retriever in CI skips when SUPABASE_URL/OPENAI_API_KEY absent; baseline is blessed on the first environment that has both.
hybrid_retriever_search_p50._ci_observation: 3 CI workflow_dispatch runs on feat/414-hybrid-latency-local-substrate (run IDs 26424907910, 26424905458, 26424903181) against the local pgvector substrate (deterministic embedder, REAL hybrid_vector_search / hybrid_fulltext_search SQL fns — NO Supabase/OpenAI, NO network) produced per-run p50 [4.23, 3.90, 3.71]ms; med-of-meds=3.90ms, stdev=0.26ms (6.7%). Absolute ms reflect Python/asyncio + local pgvector query cost on ubuntu-latest, NOT production network latency — this baseline guards CODE-latency regressions (issue #414). The 200ms _target_ms remains the documentation anchor for the production SLA.
hybrid_retriever_search_p50._tolerance_rationale: 50% relative OR 8ms absolute (whichever wider) → effective ceiling ~11.9ms ≈ 3x the 3.9ms baseline. At this small absolute scale the 8ms floor dominates, so this is INTENTIONALLY a fixed-threshold gross-regression guard (~3x), NOT a tight 2x relative guard — a true 2x slowdown (~7.8ms) would still pass. The floor is sized to absorb ubuntu-runner variance (a loaded runner can sit several ms above the 3.71-4.23ms bless range) so the gate does not flake, while still catching gross regressions (broken dense/sparse concurrency, an N+1, or a blocking call → ≥3x). Derived from the #414 substrate runs, NOT the PR #401 placeholder defaults.

hybrid_retriever_search_p95._target_rationale: Tail-latency budget: p95 should not exceed 2.5x the p50 target (200ms). 500ms is a conservative tail-latency ceiling for a 3-stream fused search.
hybrid_retriever_search_p95._ci_observation: Same 3 CI runs as hybrid_retriever_search_p50 (IDs 26424907910, 26424905458, 26424903181). Per-run p95 [9.90, 9.09, 8.94]ms; med-of-meds=9.09ms, stdev=0.52ms (5.7%). Local-substrate measurement (no network); guards code-latency tail regressions, not the production 500ms SLA (_target_ms).
hybrid_retriever_search_p95._tolerance_rationale: 50% relative OR 12ms absolute (whichever wider) → effective ceiling ~21ms ≈ 2.3x the 9.09ms baseline. As with p50, the absolute floor dominates at this scale: a fixed-threshold gross-regression guard sized to absorb ubuntu-runner variance (the p95 tail is slightly noisier than p50, hence the larger floor), NOT a tight 2x relative guard. Derived from the #414 substrate runs.

bm25_build_1k._ci_observation: 3 CI runs produced per-run median_ms [20.55, 21.08, 21.07]; med-of-meds=21.07ms, stdev across runs=0.30ms (1.42%), range across 9 individual timings=2.01ms (20.44–22.45). Build time for 1000-doc corpus via the reference Python BM25 implementation; corpus repeats from synthetic_corpus.jsonl to fill the slice.
bm25_build_1k._tolerance_rationale: 10% relative OR 5ms absolute (whichever wider). Comparison helper takes max(rel, abs) so effective band is 5ms = 23.7% of baseline. Re-verified against the 2026-08-06 fleet-aware 9-run sample (issue #1502, see _bm25_band_recalibration): max observed run-median elevation above the blessed center was +1.59ms (run 31059008024, the uniformly-slow machine); 2x that = 3.2ms, still under the 5ms min floor, so the band is UNCHANGED — at 1k the working set fits runner caches and fleet hardware differences barely register. Fleet cross-run stdev 8.46% is dominated by one uniformly-fast machine on the auto-pass side of the one-sided gate.

bm25_build_5k._ci_observation: 3 CI runs produced per-run median_ms [107.94, 111.19, 111.10]; med-of-meds=111.10ms, stdev across runs=1.85ms (1.66%), range across 9 individual timings=6.33ms (106.80–113.14).
bm25_build_5k._tolerance_rationale: 10% relative OR 20ms absolute (whichever wider). Comparison helper takes max(rel, abs) so effective band is 20ms = 18.0% of baseline (rel band 11.11ms is dominated by the abs floor). Widened from 15ms on 2026-08-06 (issue #1502, see _bm25_band_recalibration): the fleet-aware 9-run sample put the max run-median elevation above the blessed center at +9.78ms (run 31059008024, uniformly ~9% slower machine — it cleared the old 15ms band by only 5.2ms); abs band = 2x that elevation = 19.6ms, rounded up to nearest 5ms = 20ms. The 3-run blessing stdev of 1.66% under-sampled fleet variance (9-run cross-run stdev 8.28%).

bm25_build_10k._ci_observation: 3 CI runs produced per-run median_ms [224.85, 222.14, 216.50]; med-of-meds=222.14ms, stdev across runs=4.26ms (1.92%), range across 9 individual timings=12.21ms (215.35–227.56).
bm25_build_10k._tolerance_rationale: 10% relative OR 60ms absolute (whichever wider). Comparison helper takes max(rel, abs) so effective band is 60ms = 27.0% of baseline (rel band 22.21ms is dominated by the abs floor). Widened from 25ms on 2026-08-06 (issue #1502, see _bm25_band_recalibration): the old 25ms band (11.3% effective) was tighter than GitHub-runner fleet variance at the 10k working-set size — run 31063489593 hit +28.45ms (+12.8%, a size-dependent cache/bandwidth signature: its 1k/5k slices sat AT baseline) on identical code, a spurious REGRESSION. Fleet-aware 9-run sample: max run-median elevation above the blessed center = +28.45ms; abs band = 2x that elevation = 56.9ms, rounded up to nearest 5ms = 60ms. The 10k slice is the most hardware-sensitive (largest working set spills runner caches), so it carries the widest effective band; uniform code regressions are still caught by the tighter 5k band (18.0%) and the 1k anchor. The 3-run blessing stdev of 1.92% under-sampled fleet variance (9-run cross-run stdev 9.13%).
